skill.name: usage-planner
skill.description: Check Leadsets usage and estimate what a search, enrichment, email verification, or scraping job will consume. Plan batches around the remaining quotas and reset times.
skill.summary: Turn current Leadsets quotas into a batch plan.
skill.author: leadsets

security_audit.summary: All 19 static matches are false positives for shell execution, suspicious networking, or system reconnaissance. Planning is described as free, but the search probe rule can be read as permission to run a quota-consuming search. The example also assumes email verification before any results exist.

remediation.issue: A search probe can consume quota during a planning-only request.
remediation.suggestion: Limit planning to the usage lookup. Put the search probe in the execution handoff and require explicit approval before any quota-consuming call.

remediation.issue: The plan can imply that emails are verified before enrichment returns results.
remediation.suggestion: Describe verification as a result status, not a guarantee. Tell the runner to skip repeat checks only for emails with an explicit verified status.

semantic_findings.title: Search Probe Can Exceed Planning Authorization
semantic_findings.description: A rule for every run directs the agent to try a one-result search. This conflicts with the promise that planning consumes no quota. If followed during planning, the probe sends search filters and can spend request and record quota without execution approval.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The general rule directs the agent to run the probe, but the batch step assigns it to the runner. The impact depends on which instruction the agent follows.

semantic_findings.title: Planning Example Overstates Email Verification
semantic_findings.description: The example calls emails already verified before the job runs, and the planning steps broadly advise skipping a separate check. A downstream runner could trust that claim without checking the returned status.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The example makes an unconditional claim, while the verification rule requires an explicit verified status. The rule limits the risk if the runner follows it.

content.user_title: Plan Leadsets Jobs Around Usage Limits
content.value_statement: Large Leadsets jobs can run out of records, requests, or scrape units before they finish. Use current usage balances to estimate consumption and schedule batches around quota resets.
actual_capabilities: Check five-hour request and record balances, weekly record balances, reset times, search concurrency, and available scrape units.
Estimate maximum record or scrape-unit use from the planned tools and job size.
Size batches around current capacity and reset times, with 10% headroom by default.
Flag jobs that exceed remaining Free records, weekly capacity, or available scrape units.
Provide search page sizes, concurrency limits, and retry or stop guidance for the runner.
limitations: Live usage requires a Leadsets account and a configured MCP connection or REST API access.
The output is a plan, not a completed job, and it does not verify email addresses.
Other activity on the account can change the available quota after the plan is generated.
The planner does not upgrade accounts or purchase scrape units.

prompt_templates.title: Check what is left
prompt_templates.prompt: Read my current Leadsets usage. Show what remains for search, enrichment, requests, and scraping, and when the limits reset.
prompt_templates.scenario: Check the account before choosing a job.

prompt_templates.title: Check whether enrichment fits
prompt_templates.prompt: Can I enrich 800 contacts today? Check live usage and show what fits now without running enrichment.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a paginated search
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a search for 1,500 people with 15% headroom per window. Include batch sizes, page limits, and reset times. Do not run a search probe.
prompt_templates.scenario: Plan a search with a quota reserve.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a job across multiple meters
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan 2,000 company search results, 700 contact enrichments, and 200 careers pages by Friday. Check live balances and show batch timing and hard stops. Do not run the job.
prompt_templates.scenario: Check a deadline against separate quotas.

output: Illustrative snapshot: 300 enrichment records remain in a 1,000-record window. The next reset is 14:15, and 1,600 records remain this week.
Batch plan: 200 now and 900 after the reset. Recheck usage before each batch.

output_examples.input: Can my Free account handle 200 standalone email checks?
output: Illustrative snapshot: 150 shared Free records remain.
Estimate: 200 enrichment records. The job exceeds the remaining allowance by 50 records.
Reduce the job to 150 checks or fewer, or review upgrade options before running it.

best_practices: Provide the job type, count, deadline, and any quota you want to reserve.
Refresh usage before each batch, especially when other jobs share the account.
Keep planning separate from execution and approve any search probe before it runs.
anti_patterns: Using plan defaults instead of current usage balances.
Ignoring request limits when many calls may return no results.
Treating a planning estimate as proof that an email is verified.

faq.question: Do I need a Leadsets connection?
faq.answer: Yes. Live balances require a Leadsets account and a configured MCP connection or authorized REST API access.

faq.question: Does checking usage spend my quota?
faq.answer: The usage lookup consumes neither records nor requests. A search probe is a separate call and can consume quota.

faq.question: How much headroom does the planner leave?
faq.answer: The default is 10% of the window limit. Provide a different reserve when you request the plan.

faq.question: Can I plan scraping on the Free plan?
faq.answer: No. Leadsets scraping requires a paid plan and enough scrape units.

faq.question: What if my job exceeds the weekly limit?
faq.answer: The planner flags the limit. You can spread the job across weeks or check whether Leadsets supports asynchronous processing for your job.

faq.question: Does the plan show which emails are verified?
faq.answer: No. Check the status returned by enrichment or verification during execution. Do not infer verification from the plan.
